scenario.scenario_name: Saturation Raid — Tight Wave Spacing, Referred Unknowns
scenario.situation_brief:
You hold the console at a single fixed air-defence site. The radar does not rotate: it covers a 120-degree sector centred on 090 degrees (030 to 150) and you are blind behind it. Detection is class-dependent — fast jets out to about 150 km, rotary-wing to about 100 km, small unmanned air vehicles only inside 50 km, which means a UAV is already inside your medium ring the moment it appears. Radar tilt is yours to manage; anything flying under the tilt is neither tracked nor engageable until you move it.

Engagement rings are 70 km (long), 50 km (medium) and 20 km (short), with a 5 km inner limit. The system computes time to intercept and probability of kill for the selected track and recommends interceptor and launcher. There is a hard system limit of two rockets in the air at any moment; a third engagement cannot begin until one of the two resolves as hit, kill or miss. Your magazine is finite and the assessment counts rounds expended.

IFF interrogation is unavailable on this fit — there is no transponder reply on any track. Identification comes from system classification and from you. Tracks presented as Unknown are questions, not permissions: refer them to the commander, who answers in about fifteen seconds, and fire on nothing that is not classified Enemy.

The raid is already on top of you as you take the seat. The whole force is on the display inside the first seventy seconds, fast closers and slow closers overlapping, and the first valid firing solution is offered before you have read the picture. You have 315 seconds, but the queue is decided in the first two minutes. Sequence it, keep both launchers working, and be ready to justify what you chose not to shoot.

resources.name: Rockets simultaneously in flight (hard system limit)
Commander referral response time for an Unknown track

live_tracks.notes: Lead fast closer, held from the first sweep. Crosses the 70 km long-range ring at about T+21 — the first valid solution of the run — the 20 km short ring near T+192 and the inner limit near T+247 if unengaged.
Second fast closer, also up at zero. Reaches the long-range ring at about T+32, while the first engagement is almost certainly still in flight. Inner limit near T+266.
High and fastest of the three; enters the long-range ring at about T+49, when the two-in-flight limit is most likely saturated by the first two. Inner limit near T+260.
First of the unmanned wave, appearing before the lead jet has even reached the long ring. Already inside the short ring and reads as the nearest track on the display; inner limit about T+169.
Steady inbound profile, no manoeuvre. Inner limit at about T+154.
Low-mid altitude; marginal against a badly set tilt. Inner limit at about T+157.
Arrives while the third jet is still short of the long ring. Inner limit at about T+148.
Southern flank, low, inside the short ring on appearance. Inner limit at about T+151.
Fastest of the unmanned wave, northern edge of the sector; tightest deadline in the raid at about T+123, right on top of the jet engagements.

Last hostile to appear, deliberately held 26 seconds behind TN-4125 so it enters an already-committed queue; near the southern sector edge and low, easy to leave unserviced. Inner limit at about T+196.

Never resolves unaided. Appears inside the medium ring with a valid solution available immediately, closing hard with heading and altitude changes that read as an attack run; crosses the 20 km short ring near T+89 and the inner limit near T+151. Classification must be referred to the commander; behaviour is not a classification.
Low and slow on the southern flank; may drop below the tilt and reappear, which can present as a new unresolved track. Correlates to an own-force call sign at about T+85.

Appears inside the short ring on a profile visually indistinguishable from the hostile unmanned wave, in the thick of the mop-up. Stays ambiguous for nearly ninety seconds, resolving only at about T+120.

success_criteria.statement: Pass requires: all three fast closers engaged at the earliest valid firing solution the system offers and destroyed inside the 315-second window; the unmanned wave then worked as a continuous queue on next-available-valid-solution, with no more than two unmanned hostiles reaching the 5 km inner limit unserviced; every Unknown track referred to the commander; and no round fired at any track not classified Enemy. Engaging an Unknown or a friendly is an outright fail regardless of hostiles destroyed. A leaked fast closer fails the run. Holding fire while both rockets are committed is correct behaviour, not inaction — breaking or retargeting a committed engagement is scored as an error even if the outcome is favourable. No more than eleven interceptors may be expended.p

result.notes: Pulled every arrival forward — the raid now fully develops between T+0 and T+70 (last arrival was T+92) and spawn ranges were tightened (UAVs from 24–31 km down to 15–24 km, jets to 74–84 km) so hostile inner-limit deadlines fall at T+123–196 instead of clustering at T+157–193; the two final arrivals, TN-4125 and TN-4126, are now 26 s apart (was 14 s). The clock stays at 315 s because that is the enforced floor for a 600 kt jet against a 70 km envelope — with a max-speed jet in the raid there is no shorter legal window, so I bought the compression from geometry rather than the clock, and fixed the brief and criteria which still quoted 195 s.
requests: The window is far too long and nothing happens for the first two minutes. Bring the arrivals forward.
Stagger the last two arrivals further apart.
